description:
Non-required nits surfaced by the code review of explorer-matrix-leaderboard-view.
No Required issues were found; all critical implementation items are correct.
This item tracks four minor polish improvements.

preserves.behavior: Compare.tsx grouped chart rendering - only adding a comment in w1
QueryHeatmap heat coloring behavior - only adding a comment in w2 and guarding an unused call in w4

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run typecheck && npm test

work_units.notes:
Compare.tsx:196-198 - grouped bar chart uses `?? 0` for null display_ms
values (queries where all runs failed).  Zero-height bars correctly
disappear visually, but the intent is non-obvious: a reader might wonder
if 0 misrepresents failed queries as "fastest."

Fix: add a one-line comment before the `?? 0`:
  // Null means all runs failed; render as 0 so bar disappears rather than
  // crashing the chart formatter.
work_units.summary: Add comment explaining ?? 0 fallback in Compare.tsx grouped chart

work_units.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:74 - filter `v > 0` silently excludes timing=0ms
(physically impossible but could occur with rounding artifacts).

Fix: add a comment:
  // Exclude zero/null cells; sub-ms values round to 0 in some runners.
work_units.summary: Document zero-timing filter intent in QueryHeatmap.tsx

work_units.notes:
manifest.ts:79-80 - HTML detection uses `contentType.includes("text/html")`.
If a real 5xx error page uses `application/json` content-type, the gzip
DecompressionStream would throw with a cryptic "DecompressionStream error"
rather than a meaningful HTTP error.

Fix: check `!res.ok` first:
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status} fetching ${url}`);
Then proceed to content-type check for Vite SPA fallback detection.
work_units.summary: Improve getBenchmarkSummary to also check !res.ok before content-type

work_units.notes:
QueryHeatmap.tsx:272 - lightnessForCell is called unconditionally even
when suppressHeat=true (single-platform view).  The result is immediately
discarded.  This is a negligible waste but could confuse a reader.

Fix: guard the call:
  const lightness = suppressHeat ? null : lightnessForCell(ms, minInCol);
work_units.summary: Suppress lightnessForCell call when suppressHeat is true
